newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Life hopes for resolution to sales row.
newsitem.headline: Irish Life hopes for resolution to sales row.

text.p: Irish Life Plc said on Tuesday that it was still hoping for a resolution to a 15-month old dispute over its sales structure which led the company to suspend 120 of its field sales force staff on Monday.

The life assurance and investment group is meeting a further 120 staff today to ask them to accept Labour Court recommendations aimed at solving the dispute and if they don't, they too will be suspended without pay.
"Basically we are putting the Labour Court recommendations to them and asking them to indicate they will cooperate with them on an individual basis," a company spokesman said.

"If they refuse we believe that given that the dispute is 15 months ongoing, given that they reject a Labour Court offer as opposed to just something from ourselves, we believe that we now have to introduce the changes," the spokesman said.
"We regard them as normal working practices and if they refuse to cooperate with the new working situation we are advising them that they are suspended."

Irish Life's field sales force staff numbers about 400 and over 300 are members of the Manufacturing Science Union (MSF) which voted last week by almost four to one to reject the Labour Court recommendations.

Irish Life said it would meet the remaining non-union members of staff over coming days while it is currently in talks with SIPTU, which represents around 40 of the sales force, to assess their view of the Labour Court recommendations.
"We are in the very early days, we are 24 hours into the situation. We are monitoring it very closely to see what develops and we will take what action we feel is appropriate," the spokesman said.
"But our hope is for a resolution and we believe the key to that resolution is the Labour Court Recommendation."
MSF says it is rejecting the Labour Court recommendations because they compensate only 30 percent of its members.
It wants sales staff to be properly compensated for changes in their work practices and structures and wants a full technology agreement and assurances on job security.
Irish Life said it would be prepared to talk to MSF but only if it felt real progress could be made.

"Our preference obviously is not to be in this situation and if we can work with MSF to resolve it, we would be delighted. But we have worked for 15 months to try and prevent this happening and we would need very clear evidence that discussions were going to be meaningful," the spokesman said.
